text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000394 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity stratum, including many 0-1 condition visits, but documentation is too thin to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern leans toward concern. The excess 99215 share holds across every chronic-condition band in the by-complexity table, not only among sicker patients. A third of the provider's 99215s fall on patients with 0 or 1 conditions, and the sampled low-complexity claims carry minor diagnoses that rarely warrant high-complexity MDM, such as upper respiratory infection, UTI, rash or follow-up exam (e.g., C0195484, C0196828, C0196127, C0196139). The sampled high-complexity 99215s (e.g., C0196494, C0196541) look clinically plausible, so part of the panel may genuinely be complex. The records review cannot settle the question: only one documented 99215 came back (C0196708, supported), and the single data-reviewed note without a lab line is weak evidence at most. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for the low-complexity 99215s cited, to test whether the MDM and minutes support the billed level, before drawing any conclusion."}
